doc.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001

title: Worst date: Jerry Dodgion and 'Butter' with the Alden-Barrett quintet
summary: A tune falls apart on the band's first night.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Can you recall one of your worst dates ever?

How much time you got? I’ve had some embarrassing moments. The first night that the Alden-Barrett quintet worked, Chuck Wilson had to send in a sub. He had something he couldn’t get out of. And Jerry Dodgion came in and Jerry made the rehearsal, and Jerry had written a tune called “Butter” dedicated to Quentin Jackson. And I had a bunch of parts of it around, and I had like two pages of a two part, I had two copies of page one and two copies of page two and I put one and one together and taped them together and put them up on the bandstand. And it was the first night of the existence of the band. And I got to the bottom and I went back up to letter A, and the tune blew up in mid air. It felt like a house of cards and we stumbled like a two-legged racehorse to the finish line and crawled across on our face and finished. And Jerry Dodgion turned around and looked at us and looked mostly at me and said, “Thanks guys, that was beautiful, just perfect.” Big smile on his face. And we were all laughing. That was pretty horrible. And there have been things like that. But I haven’t had — I’ve had precious few gigs that I really despised. There’ve been a few. I mean circumstances will — somebody in the audience, especially if you’re doing a party for somebody and it’s a private party.
